note: Divergence ratchets and depth floors for scripts/flix-spec-conformance.mjs. Lower a ratchet or raise a floor as the grammar improves; never move either the other way without saying why in the commit message. The measurement is only comparable against the flix-spec inputs recorded below -- a different pin or fixture revision is a different question, not a regression. scripts/flix-spec-conformance.mjs refuses a checkout whose artifact version, pin, vocabulary digests or fixture revision differ from `measuredAt`; pass --remeasure to measure a new release. Three ratchets, one per derived lane: `divergences` gates structure modulo error recovery, `recoveryDivergences` gates error-recovery shape on its own, and `diagnosticDivergences` gates accept/reject agreement. Each lane also has a depth floor (`depthFloor`, `recoveryDepthFloor`, in percent), because unmapped nodes are skipped rather than compared: agreement once fell from 122 to 107 when the mapping set was completed, while depth rose 84% to 90%. A divergence count that falls together with depth is the number to distrust, and the floor is what fails the build on it.

oracle_conformance.comment: Re-measured against flix-spec 0.77.1, which pins Flix v0.77.0: a different question from the 0.75.8 baseline, not a regression against it. The suite grew 138 -> 147 fixtures and flix-spec's transparency now fires per occurrence, so canonical trees are about half their former size. Of the 101 divergences, 70 fall in fixtures that already existed (61 before) and 31 in the nine new ones -- most of those are syntax this grammar does not yet parse: `use pkg::...` package paths, effect type parameters, and the new match/ematch recovery shape. The four `elide` entries flix-spec now removes centrally (Expr.Expr, Pattern.Pattern, QName, UsesOrImports.UseOrImportList) were deleted with identical results; ModifierList and AnnotationList stay, because `elide-empty` keeps their one-child occurrences and removing them measured +48 divergences. `java_qualified_name` joined `ignored`, symmetric with `qualified_name`: a single-segment Java name is a bare Ident in the canonical tree (fixes try-catch). Then lowered 101 -> 85 by grammar work: `use pkg::...` package paths (the new `package` node, mapped to UsesOrImports.Package), effect type parameters, and generic effect operations parsed structurally as the reference parser does. nodesUnmapped rose 13 -> 17 because the package-path fixture reaches four more aliased_name nodes, which were already unmapped. Raised 85 -> 86 when law declarations and the lawful modifier were removed from the grammar (retired upstream at v0.75.2): the negative law fixture is now rejected, as by the reference, and tree-sitter's ERROR keeps the `lawful` name as a child where the reference's ErrorTree holds only a token.

recovery_conformance.comment: Error-recovery shape alone, over the 28 fixtures whose raw reference tree contains a recovery marker (22 before). All 47 divergences in the previously measured fixtures are unchanged; the 9 new ones sit in new negative fixtures -- match/ematch with a missing body, operation type parameters, and the spaced package separator. The dominant disagreement is unchanged and diagnosed in flix-spec's docs/CONFORMANCE.md: both parsers reject `1_`, and they disagree about where the error is. Lowered 56 -> 55 by the same grammar work. Two divergences remain by design: for a spaced package `::` and a generic effect operation the reference wraps the offending part in an ErrorTree inside an otherwise complete node, and this grammar parses both without a marker -- it follows the parser's tree, not its diagnostic. Raised 55 -> 56 by the same removal, which also lifted depth 63% -> 65%: the law fixture now recovers in the reference's shape -- an error for `lawful`, then a trait whose body holds an error for the `law` line -- and differs only at the leaves.

diagnostic_conformance.comment: Accept/reject only: the adapter reports one `tree-sitter.ParseError` per unit that contains an ERROR node, a MISSING token or a recovery marker, and no diagnosticMappings translates that name, so kind and line stand down -- an ERROR spans the recovery region, not the reference's error token. Parse-phase evidence only, as flix-spec's canonical set is lexer and parser errors alone. Of the 9 disagreements, 8 are units the reference rejects and this grammar accepts: two by design (a spaced package `::` and a generic effect operation, parsed as Parser2 builds them), and six grammar gaps (unterminated block comment, unterminated string interpolation, `static` as a name, a misplaced doc comment, an operator signature in a trait, an anonymous class). The ninth runs the other way: operator-error.flix, which the reference accepts and this grammar rejects.

source_invariants.comment: document-shape passes. The two vocabulary checks stand down because a projection map is in play, and token-accounting and token-positions stand down because this adapter emits no token text -- tree-sitter's named-node view has no Flix tokenization behind it. A structural profile, stated rather than implied.
